hook: A gallium-68 tungsten-oxide cluster enters cells better than free gallium-68, a possible PET cell tracer.
summary: Chemists built a tungsten-oxide cage (a Keggin polyoxometalate) holding radioactive gallium-68 and made it in under an hour. In hamster ovary cells it was taken up more than gallium chloride or gallium-oxine and showed low toxicity. Only one cell line was tested, and no animal imaging is reported.
title: A 68Ga-Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking.
